data.name: graph_fpt_weights
data.problem: Recover the edge weights of a weighted 3x3 grid graph from empirical first-passage-time distributions r'(t, x, y) of random walks observed only on the boundary vertices (inverse problem for discrete heat equations / random walks on graphs).

notes: Models may only be trained on simulated data; the test split is never used for selection

objectives: Learn a regression model from simulated data (graph_fpt) that solves: Recover the edge weights of a weighted 3x3 grid graph from empirical first-passage-time distributions r'(t, x, y) of random walks observed only on the boundary vertices (inverse problem for discrete h
Select methods by validation rel_l2 only; the test split is used exactly once, at the end
Stay within 900 worker-seconds of compute and 600 s wall time
Eliminate weak approaches with cheap feasibility checks before spending substantial compute
Constraint: Models may only be trained on simulated data; the test split is never used for selection
data.simulator_description: Random walk on a fixed {'family': 'grid', 'rows': 3, 'cols': 3} graph with 9 vertices and 12 edges; edge weights ~ U[0.2, 1.0], mu = degree, potential {'mode': 'none'}. Observed set B = [0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8] (|B|=8). Features: empirical first-passage probabilities r'(t, x, y) for t = 1..9 and (x, y) in B x B from N = 10000 walks per pair, flattened in (t, x, y) order -> 576 features. Target: weights (12 values). Inverse problem: recover graph parameters from boundary first-passage data.
